sections.overview: Reindeer, called caribou for wild populations in North America, are circumpolar deer of Arctic and subarctic regions.
sections.identification: Unlike most deer, both sexes can grow antlers, which are shed and regrown seasonally.
sections.habitat: Depending on population and season, reindeer use woodland, forest edges and open Arctic tundra.
sections.diet: They browse and graze on plants; lichens and fungi become important winter foods.
sections.behavior: Some populations make long seasonal movements between winter woodland and summer tundra.
sections.reproduction: The consulted references do not provide a single breeding schedule applicable to this geographically varied species.
sections.ecology: The name reindeer is common in Europe, whereas North American usage distinguishes wild caribou from domesticated reindeer.
sections.conservation: Conservation status varies among populations and subspecies, so this profile does not assign a single global category.
